Discharge Summary for Patient P1001

Patient: Alex Morgan (fictional — all data synthetic)
Patient ID: P1001
Date of Birth: 1958-06-14 (fictional)
Admission Date: 2024-01-17
Discharge Date: 2024-01-20
Length of Stay: 3 days
Discharging Physician: Dr. Patricia Holloway (fictional)
Primary Diagnosis: Advanced osteoarthritis, right knee (ICD-10: M17.11 — fictional coding for illustration)
Procedure Performed: Total right knee arthroplasty (total knee replacement)

Hospital Course Summary:
Patient P1001 (Alex Morgan, fictional) was admitted to Riverside General Hospital (fictional) on 2024-01-17 for elective total right knee replacement. The patient has a history of advanced osteoarthritis of the right knee with complete cartilage loss documented on preoperative imaging. Conservative management including physical therapy and intra-articular injections provided insufficient long-term relief.

Surgery was performed on 2024-01-18 under spinal anesthesia without complication. A cemented posterior-stabilized total knee arthroplasty system was implanted. Intraoperative hemostasis was achieved. The patient was transferred to the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) in stable condition with vital signs within normal limits.

Post-Operative Day 1 (2024-01-19):
The patient participated in physical therapy within 24 hours of surgery, achieving standing and weight-bearing with a walker as tolerated. Pain was managed with the prescribed multimodal regimen. Blood pressure and heart rate remained stable. No fever. INR was checked and within acceptable range for day 1 post-operatively. Wound inspection revealed a clean, dry, intact incision without erythema or drainage.

Post-Operative Day 2 (2024-01-20 — Discharge Day):
The patient ambulated independently with a walker to the end of the hallway and back without significant distress. Vital signs remained stable. Wound appeared clean. Pain was rated 4 out of 10 on the numeric pain scale at rest and 6 out of 10 with activity. The patient and the designated caregiver completed discharge education covering wound care, medication management, activity restrictions, and warning signs. The patient was able to correctly verbalize the instructions and demonstrated correct technique for lower extremity exercises.

Discharged to: Home with family support. Home physical therapy arranged starting 2024-01-22.

Current Medical History (Synthetic):
- Hypertension — managed with amlodipine 5 mg daily (pre-existing)
- Hyperlipidemia — managed with atorvastatin 20 mg daily (pre-existing)
- Advanced right knee osteoarthritis (primary indication for surgery)
- No known history of venous thromboembolism prior to this admission

Surgical Complications: None documented during hospitalization.

Discharge Condition: Good. Ambulating with walker. Pain adequately controlled. Oriented to person, place, and time. Afebrile.

Discharge Instructions Provided:
- Wound care instructions reviewed and written copy provided.
- Medication list reviewed; patient able to identify each medication, its purpose, and dosing instructions.
- Physical therapy home exercise program demonstrated and written copy provided.
- Warning signs and escalation instructions reviewed.
- Follow-up appointment confirmed: 2024-02-01 with Dr. Holloway.
- Patient instructed to call the surgeon's office or go to the emergency room if any warning signs are experienced before the follow-up appointment.

Pending Lab Results at Discharge:
- INR check scheduled 2024-01-25 at the anticoagulation clinic.

Primary Care Follow-Up:
Primary care physician Dr. Samuel Reeves (fictional) has been notified of the admission and discharge by electronic communication. Post-operative reconciliation of all medications is recommended at the next primary care visit.
